added_models.model: In-vitro cancer cell-line panel, RAS/BRAF genotype vs MEK-inhibitor sensitivity (KRAS-genotype selection of pancreatic patients)

efficacy.model: In-vitro cancer cell-line panel, RAS/BRAF genotype vs MEK-inhibitor sensitivity (trametinib)
efficacy.note: Trametinib cell-line panel: RAS/BRAF-mutant lines most sensitive; applied to pancreatic cancer as a KRAS-genotype selection hypothesis, not yet compared.
efficacy.short: RAS-mutant lines most sensitive in vitro
efficacy.quote: Potent cell growth inhibition was evident in most tumor lines with mutant BRAF or Ras.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; pan-tumour panel, pancreatic lines not itemised in the abstract. model_filed not checked against NDA 204114 PharmR in this run.
efficacy.judgement: Opener for the only patient-level prediction in the context: genotype picks responders. A different system (in-vitro immortalised-line panel) and a different prediction (who responds) from the xenograft track, so its own track; ex_vivo is the nearest model_kind.

efficacy.model: In-vitro cancer cell-line panel, RAS/BRAF genotype vs MEK-inhibitor sensitivity (trametinib)
efficacy.note: Randomised phase II pre-specified KRAS subgroups by cfDNA; KRAS-mutant patients (n=103) gained no OS from trametinib, so genotype did not pick responders.
efficacy.short: KRAS-mutant patients gained nothing from trametinib
efficacy.quote: Outcomes were independent of KRAS mutations determined by cfDNA.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Whether the KRAS-subgroup analysis appeared in the 2013-09-26 registry results posting was not checked, so year follows the paper (Crossref created 2014-06-07; print August 2014).
efficacy.judgement: The panel predicted RAS-mutant tumours as the responders; the trial tested exactly that subgroup and found no difference, a wrong patient-level prediction. Pairing: the trial cites the RAS rationale but does not set the panel beside its data.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: OS in the KRAS-mutant subgroup (no difference between arms) against predicted genotype-dependent sensitivity

patient_trials.quote: KRAS mutation-positive patients (n=103) showed no difference in OS between arms.

efficacy.model: In-vitro cancer cell-line panel, RAS/BRAF genotype vs MEK-inhibitor sensitivity (refametinib, sibling-drug panel)
efficacy.note: Single-arm phase I/II (n=90): response, PFS and OS were all higher without detectable KRAS mutation in ctDNA, the reverse of the panel's prediction.
efficacy.short: KRAS-wild-type patients did better on refametinib
efficacy.quote: Overall response rate, disease control rate, progression-free survival, and overall survival were higher in patients without detectable KRAS mutations (48% vs. 28%, 81% vs. 69%, 8.8 vs. 5.3 months, and 18.2 vs. 6.6 months, respectively).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Springer page blocked). Single-arm trial, ctDNA subgroups, unadjusted. Refametinib's own panel (Iverson 2009) states no genotype prediction in its abstract, so the model side is trametinib's panel (product_in_model false). NCT01251640 has no posted results (checker-verified), so registry_date is null; year is the online date 2016-12-14.
efficacy.judgement: Second member drug on the same patient-level prediction, now with the direction reversed (magnitude opposite). Same status as 2014, so strengthens.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: ORR 48% vs 28% and median OS 18.2 vs 6.6 months, KRAS wild-type vs mutant ctDNA

patient_trials.quote: The objective response rate was 23% and the disease control rate was 73%.

efficacy.model: In-vitro cancer cell-line panel, RAS/BRAF genotype vs MEK-inhibitor sensitivity (pimasertib, sibling-drug panel)
efficacy.note: Randomised phase II part (n=88): no benefit over placebo with gemcitabine and KRAS status did not influence PFS or OS; third member drug, same miss.
efficacy.short: KRAS status did not pick pimasertib responders
efficacy.quote: KRAS status did not influence PFS or OS.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Registry results (NCT01016483) posted 2017-06-23 per the checker; whether they carry the KRAS subgroup was not checked, so year is the online date 2018-08-09.
efficacy.judgement: Third member drug; genotype again failed to pick responders. Same status, strengthens. The track never turned: no tier 1-4 source shows a KRAS-mutant subgroup benefiting from any member drug.
efficacy.reason: Three member drugs, genotype never picked responders
efficacy.magnitude_basis: PFS and OS by KRAS status (no influence) against predicted genotype-dependent sensitivity

patient_trials.quote: PFS and OS outcomes did not indicate any treatment benefit for pimasertib over placebo in combination with gemcitabine

considered_not_added: Kinsey 2019 Nat Med PDX (trametinib + chloroquine regressed patient-derived PDA xenografts; one patient responded to trametinib + HCQ in the same paper): same system as the draft's pdac-xenograft-pdx track, so a candidate entry there, not a new track. Patient side beyond n=1: Hofmann 2024 AIO retrospective (19 patients, all PD), Yang 2023 real-world (8 patients, 0 responses), THREAD NCT03825289 terminated with no results.

Datta 2022 Gastroenterology PKT GEMM (trametinib + ruxolitinib + anti-PD-1; one patient with clinical benefit): KRAS-driven GEMM is the draft's kras-gemm-kpc system, patient side is a single case, no trial; not a new track.

Syngeneic KPC-implant immunocompetent models of trametinib + anti-PD-1 (Pham 2024 MCT, Herbst 2026 JCI): a different system from GEMM and PDX, but neither models SBRT nor compares with NCT02704156, both postdate the trial and neither states a comparison; no admissible entry.

NCT02704156 / Zhu 2022 Lancet Oncol (SBRT + pembrolizumab + trametinib vs SBRT + gemcitabine, OS HR 0.69): the trial's own rationale (EClinicalMedicine 2022 secondary analysis) cites no pancreatic model for the triple regimen and PubMed has none, so it belongs on an existing track's patient_trials, not a new track.

Patient-derived organoids (Wang 2026 Front Immunol; Grossman 2022 HOPE; Tiriac-type pharmacotyping): MEK combinations screened but organoid-patient comparisons are for chemotherapy only; no MEK-class patient comparison.
Kawaguchi 2017 Oncotarget patient-derived orthotopic xenograft (trametinib regressed a gemcitabine-resistant PDOX): no patient comparison for trametinib.

Trametinib + gemcitabine Japanese phase I/Ib ILD signal: belongs on the existing tox-species-rat-dog track. Bundle PharmR lines 400-405 state the dog 13-week lungs were a target organ (minimal hemorrhage, mononuclear infiltration, pleural fibrosis, macrophage accumulation; all minimal to mild) and that clinically trametinib has been associated with interstitial lung disease and pneumonitis - a stated tier-2 comparison for that track.

Lapatinib + trametinib phase I (Huijberts 2020, 10.1007/s00280-020-04066-4; 34 patients, 3 pancreatic; RP2R trametinib 1 mg continuous after DLTs): belongs on the existing PDX track's dose cell (Walters 2013 model side), not a new system.
Vena 2015 CCR pimasertib + gemcitabine orthotopic model: model_src for the existing PDX-track Van Cutsem entry, not a new system.
FAK inhibitor + trametinib phase II (J Gastrointest Oncol 2022): not searched further in this run (budget); its model side would be KPC GEMM work, the existing GEMM track.

In-silico / exposure-response dose models: no pancreatic-specific QSP or PK-PD dose model with a patient comparison found; trametinib's 2 mg came from mixed-tumour phase I pERK/PK already on the PDX dose cell.
